slowest_experiments.experiment: Reconcile fourteen outcomes and set evidence-based continuation rules
Bind fourteen tasks and ingest length-confounding and delayed-feedback methods
Test a length-only baseline and source permutation before crediting semantics
Repair source-intervention import receipts and qualify the real dispatcher
Preserve board continuity and bound traffic-sensitive acceleration

summary: Eight compute-bound experiments completed in 24.9 wall-time minutes (averaging 3 minutes per experiment) based on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction. Execution was led by 'Reconcile fourteen outcomes and set evidence-based continuation rules' at 4.1 minutes, 'Bind fourteen tasks and ingest length-confounding and delayed-feedback methods' at 3.87 minutes, and 'Test a length-only baseline and source permutation before crediting semantics' at 3.65 minutes, with the top five compute-bound tasks totaling 18.5 minutes (74.3% of the milestone wall time). The post-execution GPU monitor report recorded both RTX 3090 GPUs idle (5MB and 4MB allocated at 0% utilization) upon completion with gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as false, while continuous active-window accelerator telemetry was unrecorded and no multi-model task requiring DualGPURunner was present.
bottlenecks_identified: The top five compute-bound experiments ('Reconcile fourteen outcomes and set evidence-based continuation rules' at 4.1 minutes, 'Bind fourteen tasks and ingest length-confounding and delayed-feedback methods' at 3.87 minutes, 'Test a length-only baseline and source permutation before crediting semantics' at 3.65 minutes, 'Repair source-intervention import receipts and qualify the real dispatcher' at 3.55 minutes, and 'Preserve board continuity and bound traffic-sensitive acceleration' at 3.33 minutes) accounted for 18.5 of 24.9 total wall-time minutes (74.3%), but available records lack intra-task phase breakdown to isolate specific execution delays.
Milestone timing relied on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction because the live git-log path found 0 commits, omitting granular per-phase boundary markers and execution metadata.

The GPU monitor report provides only a single post-execution snapshot (both RTX 3090 GPUs idle at 0% utilization with 5MB and 4MB allocated at 2026-09-29T02:17:26.505603+00:00), leaving continuous accelerator utilization and throughput unmeasured across the 24.9 minutes.
improvements_suggested: Add granular phase-level timing within outcome reconciliation, task binding, and baseline permutation tasks to profile where execution time is concentrated.
Persist structured execution receipts at milestone boundaries to avoid falling back to disk-mtime reconstruction.
Sample GPU utilization, memory usage, and temperature periodically throughout task execution to capture active-window accelerator telemetry.
Include explicit concurrency and model count declarations in task manifests to unambiguously verify DualGPURunner applicability.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Implement intra-task phase profiling for the longest-running outcome reconciliation and task binding workflows to identify internal bottlenecks.
Persist structured milestone execution receipts to eliminate disk-mtime fallback reconstruction when git log yields 0 commits.
Deploy lightweight continuous GPU telemetry logging during compute-bound runs to measure active accelerator utilization.
meta_reflection: The GPU monitor report captured quiescent accelerators (both RTX 3090 GPUs at 0% utilization with 5MB and 4MB allocated) at milestone completion timestamp 2026-09-29T02:17:26.505603+00:00, indicating post-run idle state rather than mid-task stalling, consistent with gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=false. Without continuous active-window telemetry or intra-task phase timers for the 4.1-minute outcome reconciliation and 3.87-minute task binding tasks, specific internal compute bottlenecks cannot be definitively isolated from available records. Estimated time savings are set to 0% pending empirical measurement of phase profiling and receipt persistence tooling improvements.
